Graduate Programs
Main Content
Advance your education through a graduate degree in chemistry.
Pursuing graduate work in chemistry at TCU combines the best of both worlds. You can
work on problems of contemporary interest — from medicine to materials science — in
a setting that allows for intimate mentorship from your Ph.D. advisor.
That is, the average research group size here is two graduate students – far less
than that of R1 institutions. This environment is ideal for students that come to
graduate school with a broad liberal arts background or little research experience,
but with a passion for science.
While pursuing your degree, opportunities for professional development abound. Your
training in communication will form a foundation for presentations at regional, national
and international conferences as well as your first job talks. Working hands-on with
your Ph.D. advisor in the design of experiments or preparation of manuscripts will
hone your abilities as an independent investigator and clear communicator. Teaching
and working in a laboratory with undergraduate researchers will develop your leadership
skills.
Students graduating from the program have opportunities to enter industry or academia.
Many pursue post-doctoral work at some of the most prestigious laboratories across
the world.

Application Process
Application deadlines for the College are flexible, but apply by January 1 for maximum
consideration for Fall and Summer admission and by September 15 for maximum consideration
for Spring admission for most programs.
Application Materials
Students need to fulfill the general TCU admission requirements.
A completed online application (see below.)
Three letters of recommendation (the online application will prompt you for information
regarding your references.)
Transcripts of all colleges attended (upload unofficial copies via the online application.
If you are admitted to the program a single copy of all official transcripts will
be required – see address below) [When applicable, student needs to submit English
translations of transcripts. We do not provide this service.]
Personal Statement of Purpose (upload via the the online application. Essay – 1,000
words or less, that describes your motivation and goals for graduate study, career
ambitions, and the specific ways TCU may fit those.)
TOEFL/IELTS scores (input scores in Testing Information section in the online application,
then request official scores to be sent to TCU Graduate Studies, ETS institutional
code 6820) for evidence of proficiency in English a minimum TOEFL score of 80 (internet
based) or 550 (paper based) is required or a minimum IELTS score of 6.5].
GRE Requirements
The GRE is not required for any Department in the College of Science & Engineering.
Any submitted GRE score is part of a holistic review of each application, and original
documentation of the scores will be required if admitted.
Application Fee
Fee of $60 through the online application
For International Applications Only
TOEFL is required of all international students – applicant may request a telephone
interview with the department for possible waiver of the TOEFL.
For U.S. permanent resident: Please confirm that you are a permanent resident of the
United States by emailing a scanned copy of your green card to csegradapp@tcu.edu.
For non-permanent residents, please upload the completed International Student and
Scholar Form with your application.
International Student and Scholar Form
Admitted students will also be required to provide proof of financial support by filling
out and returning the International Student Financial Statement. Students on full
Teaching Assistantships (see below) do not have to use this form.
Financial Statement for International Students

Frequently Asked Questions
What application materials do students need to submit?
Please refer to the application process.
How many students will be accepted this year?
The number of students that are accepted depends on the number of available teaching
and research assistantships available in a given year.
Are students accepted to start in January?
We have accepted between 0–2 students to start their graduate studies in January.
However, most new graduate students start in August.
When are decisions made about acceptance into the program?
We generally make our first round of offers for fall admission around mid-to-late
February. We then typically make a second round of offers in April if there are still
positions available.
We continue to make offers at that point until the class is filled. Decisions for
spring admission are usually made in mid-to-late October.
Can I visit the Department?
Domestic students who have submitted all of their application items are certainly
welcome to visit the department. We will typically cover travel costs. Please contact
Graduate Director to arrange your visit.
What is the deadline for applying to the program?
The fall admission deadline is January 1 for primary consideration. For the spring
admission it is September 15.
Can the application fee be waived?
The $60 application fee could be waived upon request for some qualified applicants.
The contact information is listed in the application portal.
Do you offer assistantships?
All admitted students are guaranteed a stipend and tuition/fee waiver. This includes
international students. To be considered, just check the appropriate box in the application.
There are a limited number of assistantships available, so admission is competitive.
How much is the stipend for graduate students?
The current regular stipend for teaching and research assistants in the Department
of Chemistry & Biochemistry is $28,600 per year. Exceptional applicants can be considered
for an additional stipend award.
Do graduate students have to pay tuition?
Graduate Students supported by assistantships receive full tuition waivers.
Do graduate students have to purchase health insurance?
All graduate students, including international students, will be enrolled automatically
for TCU health insurance after enrollment of classes. To opt out, you must complete
a waiver form on the Haylor website. International students are required to carry
the SHI plan. Most graduate students who are receiving financial aid may be eligible
for a Health Insurance Award (HIA), covering 85 percent of the cost of the SHI plan.
Please see the Health Insurance page from the Graduate Studies.
Is the GRE required?
No, we do not require applicants to take the GRE. If students have taken the exam,
they are welcome to submit copies of their scores.
What is the GRE Institution Code for Texas Christian University?
The institution code for Texas Christian University is 6820.
What are the minimum TOEFL/IELTS scores?
TOEFL or IELTS is required for all international students. For English proficiency,
TCU’s minimum TOEFL score is 80 (internet based) or 550 (paper based), or an IELTS
score of 6.5. Applicant may request a telephone interview with the department for
possible waiver of the TOEFL or IELTS.
